newsitem.title: USA: U.S. economy expanding, prices subdued-Fed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. economy expanding, prices subdued-Fed.

text.p: The economy grew moderately over the past two months with wages and retail prices mostly subdued, the Federal Reserve said Wednesday.
In its latest summary of national economic activity, the central bank said labour markets remained tight and employers throughout the country reported shortages of qualified help.
Fed policy-makers will use the findings when they meet on May 20 to consider raising interest rates again after raising them in March for the first time in over two years.
"(The economy) generally continued to expand at a moderate rate through March and April," the Fed said in its so-called Beige Book summary of economic conditions.
The housing and construction industries remained strong, it said. Manufacturing companies ran their businesses at very high levels with some reporting big increases in new orders.

The economy's continued buoyancy does not look to have put much upward pressure on wages or prices, the Fed said. "Despite tight labour markets, upward wage pressures remained generally subdued," it said.
The Fed noted "a few new reports of upward wage pressures."
The Fed said virtually all its regional banks reported that retail prices were "relatively flat." Prices for raw and intermediate goods were said to be mixed.
"Most districts reported that prices at the retail level remained subdued," the central bank said.
The Fed's increase of a quarter point in short-term rates in March was a bid to keep economic growth moderate and ward off inflation.

Many economists expect the Fed to raise rates again when the central bank's policy-makers meet on May 20. They say the Fed wants growth of about 2 percent to 2.5 percent a year and believe sustained growth above that level could lead to inflation.
The economy grew 2.4 percent last year but the rate of growth jumped to an impressive 5.6 percent in the first quarter.

The summary was prepared by the Chicago Fed regional bank and was based on interviews with businesses before April 28. The last such survey of economic conditions in all 12 Fed regions was issued on March 12.
